question: Pulakeshin II belonged to which of the following dynasties?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Chalukya Dynasty.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chalukya dynasty **ruled large parts of **Southern and central India **between the 6th and 12th centuries.
 
• The dynasty is divided into three distinct yet related branches:
 
 
• The **Badami Chalukyas (Early Chalukyas) **(543 to 753) CE.
 
• The **Eastern Chalukyas **(624 to 1070) CE.
 
• The **Western Chalukyas (Later Chalukyas) **(973 to 1189) CE.
 
 
 
• The temple architecture in Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal (a UNESCO World Heritage site) was constructed by Chalukyas.
 
• They supported Hinduism primarily, but significant Jain influences can be seen during their tenure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandya Dynasty **ruled around the **4th century BCE to 14th century CE**. having capital initially Korkai, later Madurai (in modern Tamil Nadu).
 
• The famous **Meenakshi Temple in Madurai **is constructed by Pandyas.
 
• The Pandyas have trading relation with Roman Empire, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East.
 
• They have trading relation for **exporting pearls, spices, and textiles**.

 

 
• **Chera Dynasty: **also known as the **Keralaputras**, ruled parts of the modern-day Kerala and Tamil Nadu during the early centuries BCE to around the 12th century CE.
 
• They have capital in **Vanchi (often identified with present-day Karur), **later shifting capitals various times
 
• They have rich contributions to Tamil literature, including **the Sangam literature and Dravidian style of architecture**. 

 

 
• **Rashtrakutas: **They rule in the Deccan region, known for their military prowess and contributions to art and culture ruled for (753 to 982 CE).
 
• Their** initial capital was Manyakheta (modern Malkhed in Karnataka**).
 
• They patronage Jainism and the **rock-cut Kailasanatha temple at Ellora **is an example of architecture.
 
• **Amoghavarsha I **authored works in Kannada and Sanskrit and patronized scholars and poets.
